title: Cohere and Serval storm the Sprint pack
lede: Fresh rounds lifted Cohere and Serval into the 100, and 18 companies came in while 18 slipped out. Hiring now scores in finer steps, so a few roles up or down moves a company a quarter point, not half.

sections.heading: How hiring points work
sections.body: Hiring is worth up to 2 points of a company's score, based on how many roles it has open. 1 to 2 roles earn 0.5, 3 to 5 earn 0.75, 6 to 9 earn 1, 10 to 14 earn 1.25, 15 to 19 earn 1.5, 20 to 29 earn 1.75, and 30 or more earn the full 2. No open roles, no points.

items.name: Hex
items.why: A $100M Series D at a $1.2B valuation, led by Peak XV in October, on top of 39 open roles. The biggest jump on the board, six places short of the 100.

items.name: Dust
items.why: Open roles jumped from 24 to 32, crossing the 30-role mark.

items.name: Viktor
items.why: Same 29 open roles, but the finer hiring steps now give a team that size more credit.

items.name: Simile
items.why: One more open role (9 to 10) moved it up a hiring step and back into Sprint.

items.name: Thatch
items.why: Open roles grew from 28 to 31, enough for full hiring points.

items.name: Numeral
items.why: 23 open roles now count for more under the finer steps.

items.name: Cohere
items.why: Initial close of a Series E in October, on top of 122 open roles.

items.name: Serval
items.why: A $150M Series C led by Sequoia in October, with 64 open roles and plans for 500+ hires.

items.name: Tractian
items.why: A $130M round in October plus strong traction put it straight into the top 25.

items.name: Upwind
items.why: A $400M round in October. Biggest cheque of the week.

items.name: Tessera Labs
items.why: Open roles went from 26 to 30, which tips it into Sprint.

items.name: Quartermaster
items.why: Open roles fell from 11 to 8. That now costs a quarter point, but it lands just under the Sprint line, so it ranks behind every Sprint company.

items.name: Scribe
items.why: Open roles slid from 31 to 28. A quarter point, and it stays in Race.

items.name: Positron AI
items.why: Score unchanged. New Sprint entries above it pushed it just out of the 100.

items.name: Factory
items.why: Unchanged, pushed out by new entries.

items.name: Universal Quantum
items.why: Unchanged, pushed out by new entries.

items.name: Vercel
items.why: Unchanged. Every Race company now sits behind a bigger Sprint pack.

items.name: Glean
items.why: Unchanged, pushed out by new entries.

spotlight.label: Featured this week
spotlight.name: Runlayer
spotlight.tagline: The layer between your AI models and your company's apps.

facts.v: One gateway for every AI tool call, a catalog of approved agents, and usage and cost tracking.
$30M Series A in June 2026, led by Felicis with Khosla. $42M raised in total.
Gusto, Lemonade, Opendoor, AngelList, Decagon and others.
Founders built Zapier's AI and MCP products.
Microsoft, Okta and Snowflake are adding their own agent controls.

spotlight.why: Every team that builds its own internal AI platform ends up hand-wiring the same layer between the models and the apps. You want to connect them, see which one is better for what, and know which one is eating the most tokens. Runlayer sells that layer. Anyone can describe an agent in plain language and it runs with the right permissions. Early-stage and ops teams that haven't built this themselves can just plug it in.
